summary.title: The Joel Test: 12 Steps to Better Code
summary.one_liner: A quick 12-question yes/no checklist for rating a software team's engineering discipline, with the reasoning behind each question.
keywords: how to rate a software team
takeaways: Score a team by answering 12 yes/no questions, one point per yes; 12 is perfect, 10 or lower signals serious problems.
Source control, one-step builds, daily builds and a bug database are the basic infrastructure every team should have.
Fixing bugs before writing new code keeps schedules reliable and lets a team respond quickly to competitors.
Interruptions are costly for programmers, so quiet, private workspaces pay off.
Have candidates write code in interviews and run hallway usability tests with about five people.
summary.summary: Joel Spolsky presents a deliberately informal test of software team quality: twelve yes/no questions that take about three minutes to answer. Each question gets a short essay explaining why it matters, drawing on his experience at Microsoft, Excel, and other companies, and referencing sources like Peopleware. The article covers version control, build automation, daily builds, bug tracking, zero-defect practice, scheduling, specs, working conditions, tooling, testing, hiring, and usability. It is opinionated and anecdotal rather than a formal study, and the author says it is not suitable for safety-critical software.
